newsitem.title: USA: Stocks edge lower before jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Stocks edge lower before jobs data.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks drifted lower Thursday as investors took profits after the past two days' record highs and braced for Friday's September payrolls report.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 2.98 points at 5,930.99, after finishing above 5,900 for the first time Monday and setting another record Tuesday of 5,933.97.
In the broader market, declining issues outpaced gainers by 12-9 on light volume of 215 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index was 1.22 points lower at 1,234.89 and the Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks eased 1.19 points to 692.82.
"I think we're seeing some profit-taking in here because many stocks, particularly techs, have gotten back to their highs," said Peggy Farley, chief executive at Amas Securities.
With September payrolls, wages and unemployment data due Friday, analysts said investors appeared content to bide their time until the report, a key leading indicator for inflation.

Economists expect payrolls to rise 166,000 for September, a considerably slower than the 250,000 increase in August. Average hourly earnings and the U.S. unemployment rate are expected to increase marginally.
Individual issues provided most of the action, with a handful of names dominating the session.
"There continues to be some concentrated buying among Nasdaq big-cap names," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
Cisco Systems Inc. rose 1-1/8 to 65 and Intel Corp. gained 1/4 to 99-1/4 after earlier reaching a year high of 100-1/4, its first venture past 100.
Monsanto Co. jumped 2-1/2 to 41-1/8 after an analyst at PaineWebber Inc. predicted the company's third-quarter earnings would pleasantly surprise Wall Street.
Investors continued to punish companies whose earnings threatened to disappoint.
Wall Data Inc. fell 7-3/4 to 15-1/2 after warning it expected to post a loss for the third quarter.
Peak Technologies Group Inc. fell 8-1/2 to 13-1/4 and EIS International Inc. fell 5-1/16 to 7-15/16. Both companies warned that their third-quarter earnings would fall short of Wall Street estimates.
The bond market, which rose earlier, also succumbed to profit-taking before Friday's data. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell 3/32, but the yield was unchanged at 6.85 percent.
